subject: Choice of Stan targets and approximate measurement invariance

messages.author: 86bbfdb53f9ef4d1
messages.subject: Choice of Stan targets and approximate measurement invariance
parts:
Hello Drs. Merkle and Garnier-Villarreal,

I hope this email finds you both well!

Thank you so much for the development and the phenomenal updates to blavaan the last couple years, it has been an amazing package to use!

I am working on a Monte Carlo simulation with Bayesian approximate measurement invariance and had a couple of (hopefully) quick questions for you.

1.      I was looking for some documentation or information the different variations of Stan that can be used as a ‘target = …” in bcfa() (i.e., Stan, Stanclassic, and Stancond). Are the variations due to the underlying code that blavaan creates to send to Stan? Would different results be expected depending on which version is used? I have run some tests and they seem to be very close (after setting the seed argument) but wanted to double check.

2.      For Bayesian approximate measurement invariance within blavaan, I saw the example code that Dr. Garnier-Villarreal posted (https://groups.google.com/g/blavaan/c/wBrkGIpgtlI/m/NGVddANZAwAJ), which has been extremely helpful! Is the manual code (model excerpt below) analogous to using the wiggle argument? I ran some tests and had small differences in WAIC and LOO using blavCompare() and the individual models had results that matched (typically up to the third decimal place, but fairly different PPP). I wasn't able to get the manual version to run in target = "stan", so some differences may be from that as well. I wanted to make sure that any of the results were not due to the choice in which variation was used.

mod2_ap_stan <- '

Positive =~ prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[1,1,1],.01)"))*PosAFF1 +

            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[2,1,1],.01)"))*PosAFF2 +

            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[3,1,1],.01)"))*PosAFF3

Agency =~ prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[4,2,1],.01)"))*Agency1 +

            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[5,2,1],.01)"))*Agency2 +

            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[6,2,1],.01)"))*Agency3

Positive ~~ c(1, NA)*Positive

Agency ~~ c(1, NA)*Agency

            '

Thank you so very much for your time!

All the best,

-Eric

messages.subject: Re: Choice of Stan targets and approximate measurement invariance
parts:
Eric

If done with equivalent code, all Stan variations should get similar results. They wont be exactly the same because there is also MCMC sampling variations, but they should be very similar

The code you referneced, I posted when the wiggle argument was not yet available, we strongly recommend to use the wiggle argument. I would expect blavcompare to give similar results, how different are the ppp? I already dont trust it much, as it has shown to be very variable, and not a reliable metric of model perfomance

Here are the same examples using the wiggle argument, if the wiggle metric is the same as the SD in the preious example, should be equivalent models

#########################
### configural invariance
mod1 <- '
Positive =~ PosAFF1 + PosAFF2 + PosAFF3
Agency =~ Agency1 + Agency2 + Agency3
            '

## Stan
fit1_stan <-  bcfa(mod1, data=dat, std.lv=T, group="Gender",
              n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
              sample=1000, target="stan")

#########################
### weak invariance
mod2 <- '
Positive =~ c(l1,l1)*PosAFF1 + c(l2,l2)*PosAFF2 + c(l3,l3)*PosAFF3
Agency =~ c(l4,l4)*Agency1 + c(l5,l5)*Agency2 + c(l6,l6)*Agency3

## Stan
fit2_stan <-  bcfa(mod2, data=dat, std.lv=T,
              group="Gender",
              n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
              sample=1000, target="stan")

#######################
#### Approximate weak invariance

#######
####### wiggle argument
#######
mod2 <- '
Positive =~ c(l1,l1)*PosAFF1 + c(l2,l2)*PosAFF2 + c(l3,l3)*PosAFF3
Agency =~ c(l4,l4)*Agency1 + c(l5,l5)*Agency2 + c(l6,l6)*Agency3

fit2_ap_stan <-  bcfa(mod2, data=dat, std.lv=T,
                      group="Gender",
                      n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
                      sample=1000, target="stan",
                      wiggle=c("l1","l2","l3","l4","l5","l6"),
                      wiggle.sd = 0.05)
                      #wiggle.sd = c(0.05,0.05,0.05,0.01,0.01,0.01) )

#########################
### strong invariance
mod3 <- '
Positive =~ c(l1,l1)*PosAFF1 + c(l2,l2)*PosAFF2 + c(l3,l3)*PosAFF3
Agency =~ c(l4,l4)*Agency1 + c(l5,l5)*Agency2 + c(l6,l6)*Agency3

Positive ~c(0,NA)*1
Agency ~c(0,NA)*1

PosAFF1 ~c(i1,i1)*1
PosAFF2 ~c(i2,i2)*1
PosAFF3 ~c(i3,i3)*1
Agency1 ~c(i4,i4)*1
Agency2 ~c(i5,i5)*1
Agency3 ~c(i6,i6)*1
            '


## Stan
fit3_stan <-  bcfa(mod3, data=dat, std.lv=T,
              group="Gender",
              n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
              sample=1000, target="stan")

#########################
###### Approximate Strong Invariance


#######
####### wiggle argument
#######
mod3 <- '
Positive =~ c(l1,l1)*PosAFF1 + c(l2,l2)*PosAFF2 + c(l3,l3)*PosAFF3
Agency =~ c(l4,l4)*Agency1 + c(l5,l5)*Agency2 + c(l6,l6)*Agency3

Positive ~c(0,NA)*1
Agency ~c(0,NA)*1

PosAFF1 ~c(i1,i1)*1
PosAFF2 ~c(i2,i2)*1
PosAFF3 ~c(i3,i3)*1
Agency1 ~c(i4,i4)*1
Agency2 ~c(i5,i5)*1
Agency3 ~c(i6,i6)*1
            '
fit3_ap_stan <-  bcfa(mod3, data=dat, std.lv=T,
                         group="Gender",
                         n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
                         sample=1000, target="stan",
                         wiggle=c("i1","i2","i3","i4","i5","i6"),
                         wiggle.sd = 0.05)

messages.subject: Re: Choice of Stan targets and approximate measurement invariance
parts:
Hi Dr. Garnier-Villarreal,

Thank you so very much for this extremely helpful information and for the example code. Glad to hear that you strongly recommend using the wiggle argument, that helps solidify things for the simulation. I also greatly appreciate the code examples, extremely helpful! That is good to know about PPP, I will keep that in mind as well. The PPP for the manual model was .184 while the model with the wiggle argument (wiggle.sd = .01) was .426. I had used a slightly smaller SD for the wiggle metric, when I changed the wiggle.sd to .05 based on your code the PPP was .471.

Thank you again!

All the best,

-Eric

messages.subject: Re: Choice of Stan targets and approximate measurement invariance
parts:
Eric

Sounds good. I know these ppp seem very different, but they are within the variability range that I have seen, dont seem as too variable (based on what it is). Also, a quick reminder that the ppp is not a comparison metric, and should not be use to compare models
An issue with approximate invariance is the wiggle.sd, as this can determine if the model allows to find the missed parameter, or if it too strict

Jorgensen, T. D., Garnier-Villarreal, M., Pornprasertmanit, S., & Lee, J. (2019). Small-variance priors can prevent detecting important misspecifications in Bayesian confirmatory factor analysis. In M. Wiberg, S. Culpepper, R. Janssen, J. González, & D. Molenaar (Eds.), Quantitative psychology: The 83rd annual meeting of the Psychometric Society, New York, NY, 2018 (Vol. 265, pp. 255–263). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-01310-3_23

take care
